On May 4,1943 VIII Bomber Command Mission No. 54 attacked the Ford and General Motors plants at Antwerp, Belgium. 79 B-17s of the 1st Bombardment Wing were assigned, with another 33 staging a diversion off the coast. Each B-17 was loaded with five 1,000-pound (453.6-kilogram) high explosive bombs. 65 B-17s reached the target and dropped 161.5 tons (146.5 metric tons) of high explosive bombs from an altitude of 23,500 feet (7,162.8 meters). They expended 21,907 rounds of .50-caliber machine gun ammunition and claimed ten enemy fighters destroyed and one damaged. The mission lasted 4 hours, 30 minutes.Results were considered very good.

After his wife, Carole Lombard, had been killed in an airliner crash, 16 January 1942, world-famous movie actor Gable enlisted in the Army Air Corps intending to become an aerial gunner on a bomber. Soon after enlisting, though, he was sent to Officer Candidate School and after graduating was commissioned a second lieutenant. Gable was then sent to aerial gunnery school and following that, to photography training.
